reason: Experimental: exact 4.7 source review found that native duplication after WPrism Capture copies the original _wprism_uuid unless the operator has explicitly excluded that key. Existing conformance clones only before first Capture, so its settings, _dp_original, role-provider, deletion, lifecycle and round-trip evidence does not establish the managed-cloning workflow. Production authorization is withdrawn until that identity boundary and its native recovery workflow have complete evidence.

unsupported.reason: The default native metadata copier includes _wprism_uuid. A clone of an already-managed post therefore creates conflicting embedded identity, and WPrism refuses rather than choosing an owner. There is no reviewed automatic repair or general identity-fork command. Neither an implicit blacklist change nor pre-Capture-only cloning establishes support.

In-progress Rewrite & Republish workflow state is target-sovereign and is neither migrated nor cleaned when a separately-authored duplicated post is deleted; the exact conformance profile proves those bytes remain untouched, including malformed and dangling values.

WPrism can remove authored provenance and ordinary duplicated-post entities, but it does not invoke the plugin's republish/delete-copy workflow or synthesize cleanup for an active Rewrite & Republish session.
WPrism v1 and the role-capability provider refuse multisite; network role maps and network activation state are outside this adapter.
